title: arXiv Physics — Daily notable papers, 19 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This is an inferred ordering of notable recent papers, not a readership or download ranking. The selected papers have only one or two current Semantic Scholar citations apiece and no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signals, so popularity evidence is limited. The report intentionally follows the supplied 19 November window; a newer report for the 20 November batch exists.

sections.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
sections.abstract: Dynamical averaging evolves a neural-network quantum state or observable in real time to suppress ground-state observable errors quadratically in the state error, demonstrated on non-integrable spin models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove up-to-quadratic suppression of errors in arbitrary ground-state observables and demonstrate faster convergence and lower correlation-function and magnetization errors in 1D and 2D non-integrable spin models.
sections.evidence_type: computational; theoretical error analysis and numerical non-integrable spin-model tests
sections.unique_caveat: The Schrödinger-picture method requires real-time state evolution, which can be costly; the cheaper Heisenberg approximation assumes support predominantly on a few low-energy eigenstates and can incur additional errors or instabilities when that assumption fails.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 2.947; Semantic Scholar current citations 2 (score component 2.197), 3 cross-lists (component 0.750); no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Numerical Implementation and Tests of the Quadratic Effective Action for Lorentzian Spinfoam Amplitudes
sections.abstract: The authors implement and numerically test a quadratic effective-action approximation for Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes on several triangulations, including a 24-simplex hypercube.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the quadratic action reproduces the Regge action and its curvature correction in the tested cases, and matches the nonlinear complex-critical-point action through cubic-order remainders for finite edge-length perturbations.
sections.evidence_type: computational; Julia implementations tested on double-Δ3 and 1–5 Pachner complexes, a refinement, and a 24-simplex hypercube
sections.unique_caveat: The results are a local perturbative expansion around one flat real critical point; other critical points and integration-domain boundary contributions are neglected, as are subleading 1/J terms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 2.329; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386), 1 influential citation (component 0.693), and 1 cross-list (component 0.250); no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Theory of Particle Scattering on Superconducting Qubits: From Single Devices to Quantum Arrays
sections.abstract: The authors model finite-momentum particle scattering from superconducting qubits and project sensitivity to eV–keV bosonic dark matter, including possible collective enhancement in coherent qubit arrays.
sections.claimed_result: For a modeled Xmon transmon, the authors find improved projected low-mass sensitivity; independent qubits give a rate proportional to N, while suitably prepared spatially coherent Dicke states can approach N² scaling.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; device-response calculation for a planar Xmon-style transmon and dark-matter sensitivity projections
sections.unique_caveat: The sensitivity is projected, not an observed signal; it depends on the modeled device response, and the near-N² collective enhancement requires maintained spatial coherence and suitable Dicke-state preparation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 2.329; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386), 1 influential citation (component 0.693), and 1 cross-list (component 0.250); no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
sections.abstract: Grammatical evolution over a decoder-specific language finds quantum LDPC belief-propagation decoders with improved time–logical-error trade-offs.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report evolved decoders that reduce logical errors or runtime relative to specified BP+OSD baselines and generalize across tested noise levels, code sizes, and round counts.
sections.evidence_type: computational; decoder simulations on quantum low-density-parity-check codes using a DSL and grammatical evolution
sections.unique_caveat: The reported gains are benchmark results in the tested code and noise settings; the preprint does not demonstrate real-time deployment on a quantum processor.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 2.136; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386), 3 cross-lists (component 0.750); the arXiv comment notes NeurIPS 2026 EvoRobust Workshop acceptance; no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
sections.abstract: An end-to-end physics-informed neural reconstruction and inversion method estimates tissue shear-wave speed directly from undersampled MR elastography k-space data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a 30% lower NRMSE than total-variation minimization and accurate SWS mapping at acceleration factors up to 19, with evaluation on retrospective brain data and in-vivo data.
sections.evidence_type: computational; retrospective highly undersampled brain MR elastography data, comparison with total-variation minimization, and in-vivo evaluation
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison is tied to the studied data and reconstruction setup; broader prospective and multi-site validation is not established in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.886; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386), 2 cross-lists (component 0.500); the arXiv comment gives a journal DOI and public code; no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method
sections.abstract: A lattice-based search of 15 years of Fermi-LAT data finds the isolated 261-Hz gamma-ray pulsar PSR J1622−7204 using about ten CPU hours.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report the first gamma-ray pulsar discovery using their lattice-based method and contrast its roughly ten CPU hours with about 600 CPU-years spent by an earlier semicoherent search that did not find the source.
sections.evidence_type: observational; computational lattice search of Fermi-LAT Pass 8 photon-arrival data and source-probability weights
sections.unique_caveat: The authors estimate success in only about 1% of random 80-photon subsets; the demonstrated search assumes an isolated pulsar and a simplified pulse profile, while binary-pulsar searches remain prospective.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.636; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386) and 1 cross-list (component 0.250); the paper has a Physical Review Letters reference and DOI; no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Classical Oracle Separation of QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy and Quantum Cryptography Even When P = QCMA
sections.abstract: In the query-complexity model, a new codeword-hash-pairs-in-noise problem yields a classical-oracle separation of QMA from the QCMA hierarchy and enables quantum cryptographic primitives in a relativized setting.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves an oracle-relative separation in which P, BQP, QCMA, and the QCMA hierarchy coincide while QMA is strictly stronger, and constructs specified quantum cryptographic primitives relative to such an oracle.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; query-complexity proofs in a classical-oracle model
sections.unique_caveat: These are relativized complexity-theory results; an oracle separation does not by itself establish the corresponding unrelativized separation or practical cryptographic construction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.636; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386) and 1 cross-list (component 0.250); the arXiv comment notes submission to STOC’27; no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part II: scale-by-scale budget and mesoscale self-similarity
sections.abstract: A scale-by-scale analysis of deep convective self-aggregation finds an inverse energy cascade mediated by mesoscale circulations and a self-similar frozen-moist-static-energy variance scaling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive a generalized Yaglom relation and report FMSE variance scaling approximately as r^(6/5), with departures below 100 km and below 750 m elevation; horizontal-velocity scaling retains height dependence.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; generalized structure-function and scale-dependent budget analysis of deep convective self-aggregation
sections.unique_caveat: The reported power laws break down at small horizontal scales below 100 km and below 750 m, and the velocity scaling retains residual height dependence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.636; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386) and 1 cross-list (component 0.250); no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Topological (in)equivalence encoded in zeros of wavefunction overlaps
sections.abstract: The authors encode relative topology of two-dimensional gapped band structures in phase-winding charges at zeros of the determinant of occupied-state overlaps.
sections.claimed_result: For class A, the total zero charge equals the Chern-number difference; for class AII, the parity of charge in half the Brillouin zone gives the relative Z2 invariant, illustrated in Haldane, Kane–Mele, and Qi–Wu–Zhang models.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; topological band-theory derivation and model examples
sections.unique_caveat: The construction is developed for gapped band structures in specified symmetry classes; it is a theoretical classification framework, not an experimental measurement of a material.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.636; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (component 1.386) and 1 cross-list (component 0.250); no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.

sections.title: Hydrodynamic modeling of liquid metal field emitter deformation under combined RF and DC magnetic fields
sections.abstract: Hydrodynamic and magnetohydrodynamic simulations examine how combined RF and DC magnetic fields deform a liquid-copper field emitter in accelerator cavities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find in their simulations that sufficiently high local RF electric fields can deform the emitter and potentially eject hot copper droplets into the cavity, a proposed contributor to RF breakdown.
sections.evidence_type: computational; COMSOL Navier–Stokes, electromagnetic-field, and level-set simulations of a liquid-copper emitter
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed droplet-emission mechanism is simulation-based and has not been established here by direct observation in an operating RF cavity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.386; Semantic Scholar current citations 1 (score component 1.386); the arXiv comment says the work was submitted to Physical Review Accelerators and Beams; no matching Hugging Face upvote or Hacker News discussion signal.
